questions.question: A new referral workflow is failing because staff do not know who owns abnormal results. What is the best leadership response?
choices: Tell everyone to communicate better
Define roles, decision rights, backup coverage, escalation, and a closed-loop completion signal with the people who perform the work
Add a longer policy without observing workflow
Wait for another adverse event
questions.explanation: Ambiguous ownership is a system hazard. Effective leadership clarifies who decides, acts, receives backup, escalates, and confirms closure.

questions.question: Which statement best describes psychological safety?
choices: No one receives corrective feedback
All decisions require unanimous agreement
People can ask questions, admit uncertainty, and raise concerns without humiliation or retaliation while standards and accountability remain
The team avoids difficult conversations
questions.explanation: Psychological safety enables candor and learning; it is compatible with high standards, fair accountability, and constructive feedback.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a clinical huddle?
choices: Rapidly update the shared plan when the situation, risks, workload, or resources change
Conduct annual performance reviews
Replace all medical documentation
Determine who should be blamed
questions.explanation: A huddle helps the team re-establish a shared mental model and modify the plan as conditions change.

questions.question: Which situation is primarily an adaptive challenge?
choices: Replacing a broken keyboard
Installing an approved software patch
Printing a new checklist
Changing long-standing beliefs, authority, and role expectations about who owns abnormal results
questions.explanation: Adaptive work involves identity, relationships, priorities, power, or behavior; a technical fix alone will not resolve it.

questions.question: What is the best use of SBAR?
choices: To document an entire lifetime history
To communicate a focused situation, relevant background, assessment, and clear recommendation or request, then confirm the response
To avoid stating clinical judgment
To replace emergency activation
questions.explanation: SBAR structures concise, actionable communication but still requires judgment, urgency, a clear request, and closed-loop confirmation.

questions.question: A team member raises a safety concern that is dismissed by hierarchy. What should the FNP do?
choices: Remain silent to preserve harmony
Discuss it only after discharge
Use clear graded assertion and the authorized chain of command or emergency pathway if danger persists
Post about the conflict online
questions.explanation: Hierarchy does not override patient safety. Graded assertion and escalation help make risk explicit and obtain action.

questions.question: Which action best reflects co-design?
choices: Engage affected patients and frontline staff while the problem, workflow, and solution are still changeable and show how input changes the plan
Announce the final decision and request endorsement
Invite only senior leaders
Collect feedback after full implementation without revising anything
questions.explanation: Co-design gives people meaningful influence before decisions are fixed and integrates patient and work-as-done knowledge.

questions.question: How should a leader respond to repeated incivility that affects patient safety?
choices: Normalize it as a strong personality
Praise the person privately and ignore the behavior
Move the affected employee without investigation
Protect immediate safety, document objective behavior through proper channels, support fair review, address system factors, and prevent retaliation
questions.explanation: Professional conduct and patient safety require consistent standards, objective reporting, fair process, and protection from retaliation.

questions.question: What is the best evidence that leadership training improved teamwork?
choices: Participants enjoyed the slides
Observed team behavior and patient, process, safety, workload, and equity outcomes improve and remain better over time
Every employee received a certificate
The training had a well-known speaker
questions.explanation: Knowledge and satisfaction are proximal measures; leadership improvement should change real behavior and meaningful outcomes sustainably.

questions.question: A pilot succeeds in one clinic. What should happen before spreading it system-wide?
choices: Copy it unchanged everywhere
Stop measuring because success is proven
Identify core functions, assess new context and capacity, adapt the form, retest under varied conditions, and monitor outcomes and burden
Depend permanently on the original champion
questions.explanation: Spread requires local adaptation and new testing because staffing, populations, culture, and technology can alter performance.
